name: Third Branchial Cleft Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Branchial Cleft Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of recurrent lateral neck swelling or abscess typically along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle
Identification of a fistulous tract or cyst on imaging studies such as ultrasound, CT, or MRI
Histopathological confirmation of branchial cleft epithelial lining after excision
Fistulous tract passing from the skin or pyriform sinus to the lower neck consistent with third branchial cleft anatomy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent lateral neck swelling or abscess with imaging confirmation of a fistulous tract or cyst consistent with third branchial cleft anatomy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed surgically with histopathology; imaging plays a critical role in preoperative planning.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent lateral neck abscess along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid
searchTerms: repeated neck abscess near neck muscle
neck pus collection near muscle border

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fistulous opening in the lower neck or pyriform sinus

searchTerms: painless lump on side of neck
difficulty swallowing due to neck mass

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve irritation
searchTerms: voice changes due to recurrent laryngeal nerve

rare.symptomName: Airway obstruction due to large cystic mass
searchTerms: breathing blockage from large neck cyst
difficulty breathing due to neck swelling

rare.symptomName: Recurrent thyroiditis secondary to fistula tract
searchTerms: repeated thyroid gland inflammation from fistula
chronic thyroid infections linked to neck tract
nerve damage causing weakness or numbness
loss of function due to nerve compression

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during infection episodes (e.g., ESR, CRP)
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic mass in lateral neck
CT or MRI demonstrating fistulous tract from pyriform sinus to neck
Barium swallow revealing contrast passage through fistula
other: Histopathology showing squamous epithelial lining with lymphoid tissue in cyst wall

distinguishingFeatures: Location of cyst or fistula more commonly at the middle third of the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid
Tract passes superficial to the carotid artery, unlike third branchial cleft anomaly
Midline neck mass rather than lateral
Moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion
No fistulous tract to pyriform sinus

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging neck mass with airway compromise
Recurrent deep neck infections or abscesses
references: James A. et al. Branchial cleft anomalies: clinical and imaging features. Radiographics. 2019.
Orphanet: Third Branchial Cleft Anomaly. ORPHA:141030.
